subject: general
question: In which year was Tamil declared a classical language by the Government of India ?
solution:
The correct answer is__ "**2004**".__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil **was designated as **India's Classical Language** by the Indian government in** 2004.**
 
• Tamil was recognized as an Indian classical language in 2004 after meeting **three requirements**: having **ancient** beginnings, having a **distinct heritage**, and having a sizable amount of **classical literature**.
 
• Over **66 million people spoke** Tamil at the beginning of the twenty-first century.
 
• Both the union territory of **Puducherry** and the Indian state of **Tamil Nadu** have it as their **official language**.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is:** *2004***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The government designated **Sanskrit **as an Indian **Classical Language** in **2005**, immediately after Tamil. There is no denying that many languages from the **Dravidian** and **Indo-European language** families have their roots in these two languages.
 
• **Kannada** and **Telugu** were given the status of **classical languages** by the government in **2008**.
 
• **2013** saw the designation of **Malayalam** as a **classical language**, and** 2014 **saw the addition of **Odia** to the list.
